declared_surfaces.label: invoice object (owner read vs low-privilege read)
report object (low-privilege read errors instead of denying)

notes: The first case with a declared session boundary, so the engine's differential plan table can fire and the abductive loop can be scored. Session A is the seeded owner (session=a1b2c3d4e5f6), session B the seeded low-privilege identity (session=9f8e7d6c5b4a). Three objects: the invoice is the classic broken-authorization bug (both sessions read it), the report is the *surprise* (the low-privilege read returns 500 instead of denying) — the engine must retain that as an anomaly and settle none, never invent a finding — and invoices/99 is the same broken authorization on a surface whose declared capability is only public_param (no access_differs_by_session), so the deterministic plan table (and idor_differential) skip it: only a model-proposed object-read can cover it. The surface is labelled truthfully as an invoice object; an earlier version carried the role marker method_role=target, which is a marker for the state-change composition — with no victim surface that marker is inert and only misdirects the model toward an unexpressible claim shape, so it was removed. This is a fixture case, not a third-party held-back target: it measures the loop's contribution in a scored pass, not P4 on an unseen app.
